sources.citation: Kaul S, Yates R, Gruteser M. Real-time status: How often should one update? IEEE INFOCOM, 2731-2735 (2012).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Introduces time-average Age of Information and shows freshness objectives differ from throughput and delay. It establishes the broader age-scheduling lineage, not the Run 119 identity.

sources.citation: Kadota I, Sinha A, Uysal-Biyikoglu E, Singh R, Modiano E. Scheduling Policies for Minimizing Age of Information in Broadcast Wireless Networks. IEEE/ACM Transactions on Networking 26, 2637-2650 (2018).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Proves highest-current-age scheduling optimal in a symmetric unreliable broadcast model and develops MaxWeight and Whittle policies in general settings. It strongly limits any novelty claim for max-age scheduling.

sources.citation: Tassiulas L, Ephremides A. Stability Properties of Constrained Queueing Systems and Scheduling Policies for Maximum Throughput in Multihop Radio Networks. IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control 37, 1936-1948 (1992).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Establishes queue-state-driven maximum-weight scheduling and Lyapunov-style stability. It challenges priority language and supplies the nearest classical control framework.

sources.citation: Yang Z, Srikant R, Ying L. Learning While Scheduling in Multi-Server Systems With Unknown Statistics: MaxWeight with Discounted UCB. AISTATS, PMLR 206, 4275-4312 (2023).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Shows that learning and scheduling under unknown and nonstationary service statistics requires machinery beyond deterministic age reset. Supports the Run 119 scope limitation.

sources.citation: Cohen O, Meir R, Weinberger N. Statistical curriculum learning: An elimination algorithm achieving an oracle risk. COLT, PMLR 247, 1142-1199 (2024).
sources.supports_or_challenges: Provides current theory for curriculum sequencing in statistical learning. It underscores that scientific task scheduling depends on learning structure, not age alone.

search_conclusion: Nearest primary literature already establishes Age-of-Information, max-age, MaxWeight, Whittle, and curriculum-scheduling theories. Run 119 makes no novelty or priority claim. Its bounded contribution is an exact one-step identity applied to the current Viridis state plus an executable-policy schema audit.
